clue.text: Old price tag renewed a tiny bit

indicators.note: renewed suggests the letters of the phrase are made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An old shop label on an item has been replaced, or a price changed by a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The Higgs boson, nicknamed this by the press, is a subatomic particle, about as tiny a bit of matter as there is.

clue.text: Visit Germany and deteriorate

parts.note: to visit someone is to go to see them
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A travel plan: a trip to Germany, and things going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a plant bolting and running to seed, and figuratively a person or place letting itself decline.

clue.text: Dante's Peak is one, relaxing time's over

definitions.text: Dante's Peak is one, relaxing time's over

indicators.note: a peak is the top, so it takes the top letter of the word before it

parts.note: one can be written as the article A

indicators.note: relaxing loosens the letters of the phrase so they can settle in a new order

explanation.surface: Dante's Peak, the 1997 volcano film, signals that the easy times are finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peak' gives D, the top of Dante's; 'relaxing' rearranges TIMES OVER into STER MOVIE. Read whole, the clue also describes the film: in such a picture the relaxing is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's Peak is a 1997 Hollywood picture about a volcano erupting on a small town, a classic example of the catastrophe genre.

clue.text: Girl without parents hiding in bicycle bag

indicators.note: a girl hiding in a bag sits within it, so only the inside of the bag's word is kept, its ends dropped

parts.note: a pannier is a bag hung either side of a bicycle's rack

explanation.surface: An orphaned girl conceals herself in a cyclist's luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: The bag is a PANNIER; the girl hiding in it is the letters inside, with the end letters P and R dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Orphan Annie is the famous comic-strip and musical orphan, so a girl with no mother or father is a fair description.

clue.text: Enough bowlers available in Bristol?

indicators.note: goods available in a shop are found inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: Bristols is rhyming slang (Bristol City, titty) for breasts, so one Bristol is a TIT
bowlers are round felt hats

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether bowler hats can be bought in the city of Bristol.
explanation.walkthrough: Bristol is not the English city here: Bristols is rhyming slang (Bristol City, titty) for breasts, a British joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the phrase means that will do, nothing more is needed, so it stands for enough as an exclamation.

clue.text: Cold country, some say

indicators.note: some say marks a pronunciation that only some speakers use, so the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Qatar is a Gulf state

explanation.surface: A country that some people describe as cold.
explanation.walkthrough: QATAR, said as many British speakers say it, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mucus clogging the nose and throat is the hallmark of a head cold, so the condition can stand for the illness.

clue.text: What many in the UK suffer from is housing close to nuclear plant

indicators.note: something housing another holds it inside, so one piece goes in the other

parts.words: What many in the UK suffer from
parts.note: Europhobia, or EU phobia, is fear and dislike of the European Union, common among Brexit supporters

indicators.note: close to means the end, so the final letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A political jibe that much of Britain suffers a condition, set beside a nuclear power station.
explanation.walkthrough: The phobia is of the EU, much discussed in Brexit-era Britain; R, the end of nuclear, goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphorbias are the spurges, a large genus of plants with milky sap, including the poinsettia.

clue.text: See 28
Sexually attractive people went topless after short discussion

indicators.note: after says the topless piece comes behind the cut discussion word
short means the word is cut, here losing its last letter

parts.note: talk is discussion

indicators.note: topless removes the top, the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: After a brief chat, some attractive people stripped off their tops.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang talent is the collective word for people one finds attractive, as in eyeing up the local talent.

clue.text: National Express making one mad

parts.note: to express words is to utter them

explanation.surface: A National Express coach company slogan gone wrong, driving someone round the bend.
explanation.walkthrough: National Express is a British coach company; here the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutter is informal British slang for a crazy person, someone off their head.

clue.text: Some publicity so negative for a heavyweight

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A big name is getting a lot of bad press.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike Tyson was undisputed world heavyweight boxing champion in the late 1980s, an example of a fighter in the top weight class.

clue.text: George: "More work should finish early? Many will welcome that"

indicators.note: a host who welcomes a guest takes them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a lot means many

indicators.note: finishing early means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Utopia is the famous book by Sir Thomas More

explanation.surface: Someone named George urging that more work end early, to general approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is not the comparative but Sir Thomas More, author of the 1516 book about an ideal island; 'George' is old RAF slang.
explanation.definitionFit: George is old RAF and pilots' slang for the automatic flight-control system that flies a plane without a human hand.

clue.text: Thrilling work from old poet keeping us entertained

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other
entertained guests are taken into the house, so this piece sits inside

parts.note: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet of The Faerie Queene

explanation.surface: An Elizabethan poet's thrilling work kept the reader entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspenser is a thriller, a film or novel built to keep its audience in suspense.

clue.text: As soon as fully naked Trump comes in, a predator is what you'll get

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: once can mean as soon as, as in once you arrive

indicators.note: fully naked strips the word of every outer layer down to its single central letter

explanation.surface: A lurid picture of Donald Trump entering stripped bare, with a predator the result.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripping TRUMP completely, layer by layer, leaves only its middle letter U, which goes inside ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard of Central Asian mountains is also called by this name, a big cat that hunts wild sheep and goats.

clue.text: Plant disease caused by recreational drug (indeed, cannabis)

parts.note: E is slang for ecstasy
yes means indeed, as agreement
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A plant ailment blamed on recreational drug use, with cannabis named in brackets.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyespot is a fungal infection of cereals and other crops, marked by eye-shaped lesions on stems and leaves.

clue.text: You and I taking part in gym: a bad thing, a pest

indicators.note: joining in an activity puts one in the middle of it, so this piece goes inside the others

parts.note: PE is physical education, school gym
an evil is a bad thing
you and I together are we

explanation.surface: Two people joining a gym session describe it as a bad and pestilent thing.
explanation.definitionFit: This small beetle lays its eggs in garden pea pods, its larvae eating the seeds, making it a crop pest.

clue.text: Old bugger originally found in house? Not anymore!

definitions.text: Old bugger originally found in house? Not anymore!

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so these pieces go within the other
originally points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An old rascal who once lived in a house but no longer does.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue describes someone who used to live in a house and now does not: a homeless wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter of the American road, homeless and wandering, is exactly someone not found in a house anymore.

clue.text: In the US, it's OK to leave husband for one primarily interested in Italian food

indicators.note: to leave means a letter goes out of the word
for here means in place of, so a new letter takes the departing one's spot

parts.note: right on is an American expression of approval
one can be written as the article A

indicators.note: primarily picks out the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An American approves of leaving a husband for someone mainly interested in Italian food.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni is a ridged tube pasta, a staple dish of Italian cooking.

clue.text: Trouble arising after one in a caravan makes a bloomer

indicators.note: after places this piece behind the other

parts.note: a camel is one beast in a desert caravan

indicators.note: arising goes up, so in a down clue the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Something going wrong in a travelling caravan leads to an embarrassing blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake; here it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a flowering plant, and the camellia is a shrub prized for its showy winter flowers.

clue.text: Dalibor initially ascended mountain by foot

parts.note: Dalibor is the setter, who refers to himself as I

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: The setter climbed a mountain on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody a foot is a unit of metre, and the unstressed-stressed pair is the commonest such foot in English verse.

clue.text: Islamic stronghold's appropriate introduction to Holy Father

parts.note: to bag something is to appropriate it

indicators.note: an introduction comes first, so the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: dad is father

explanation.surface: A stronghold of Islam is properly introduced to the Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq's capital was for centuries seat of the Abbasid caliphs, the great centre of the Islamic world.

clue.text: Pop singer showing first signs of diarrhoea after eating rice dish from the East

indicators.note: eating takes food in, so one piece goes inside the other
first signs take the opening letters of the next two words
read from the East is read right to left in an across clue

parts.note: pilau is a spiced rice dish

explanation.surface: A pop star showing symptoms of a stomach upset after a takeaway rice dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a link word putting one piece behind another; its first letter A is part of the wordplay, with D from diarrhoea.
explanation.definitionFit: Dua Lipa is an English pop star with hits such as New Rules and Levitating.

clue.text: Finished with girl in Irish town

parts.note: done means finished
gal is an informal word for girl

explanation.surface: Someone has finished with a girl from an Irish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Donegal is a town in the far north-west of Ireland, which also gives its name to the surrounding county.

clue.text: US artist's former record label upset members of staff

parts.note: EMI was a British record label, now absorbed into others

indicators.note: upset turns over, so in a down clue the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: men are members of a workforce

explanation.surface: An American artist's old record company has upset its employees.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminem is the American rapper Marshall Mathers, a recording artist since the late 1990s.

clue.text: 23 people fighting alcohol must accept tax on rum, to start with

indicators.note: accepting takes something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous
VAT is value added tax

indicators.note: to start with picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Members of a temperance group must put up with a duty on rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is the solution to 23 across, MOVIE.
explanation.definitionFit: James Cameron's 2009 blockbuster Avatar, about the planet Pandora, is a film, so it fits the cross-reference.

clue.text: See 2
General Galtieri's gutted, struggling to get a drink

indicators.note: gutted has its insides removed, keeping only the outside letters
struggling suggests the letters are thrashing about into a new order

explanation.surface: Argentina's General Galtieri, devastated and floundering, reaches for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Galtieri, gutted, is GI; 'struggling' rearranges GENERAL plus GI. Galtieri led Argentina in the 1982 Falklands War.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft drink flavoured with ginger, often used as a mixer, is a fair example of a beverage.

clue.text: Brussels protecting Poles with, ultimately, positive result

indicators.note: protecting surrounds, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: Brussels stands for the EU, whose institutions are based there
N and S are the north and south poles

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: The EU shields Polish people and the outcome is good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland; it is the magnetic poles N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow as a consequence is to come about afterwards, so the verb fits result in the sense of happen as an outcome.

clue.text: Dingo a vet treated?

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters are worked on and rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild dog brought to a vet for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges DINGO A VET; read whole, the clue names the animal a vet might treat.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is Australia's wild dog, long regarded as the continent's indigenous canine.

clue.text: Capital generated by The Sound Of Music?

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is heard, so the next word is said aloud

parts.note: soul is a genre of music

explanation.surface: A capital city produced by the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Sound Of Music' looks like the musical title; split, it is the sound of a kind of music, SOUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Seoul is South Korea's capital city.

clue.text: Trading centre with little space for fur

parts.note: a mart is a market
an en is a small printer's space, half an em

explanation.surface: A market with little room for selling fur.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelt of this weasel-like animal is prized for coats, so the creature's name is used for the fur.

clue.text: Fantastic idea! Local TV presenting a 1960s film

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wildly fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic reaction to a regional television station screening an old movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellini's 1960 Italian picture with Anita Ekberg in the Trevi Fountain is the famous film of that name.
